Stop treating AI coding like a lottery and start building production-grade software with engineering discipline! 🚀

Tired of your AI coding assistant writing messy code, skipping tests, and hallucinating architecture? Superpowers transforms chaotic AI prompt engineering into a structured, autonomous software development lifecycle with rigorous TDD and subagent-driven workflows. 

The Problem: AI coding agents are notoriously unreliable out of the box. They rush into coding without planning, break existing features, and require endless hand-holding through frustrating trial-and-error prompt loops. 

Superpowers solves this by injecting a comprehensive methodology—composed of automatic skills, brainstorming, systematic planning, and test-driven development—directly into your favorite AI coding harnesses.

Notable Features:
🧠 Automatic skill triggering that forces agents to pause, brainstorm specs, and create granular implementation plans before writing a single line of code.
🤖 Subagent-driven development and parallel agent dispatching to execute multi-hour tasks with built-in two-stage reviews.
🧪 Strict enforcement of red-green-refactor Test-Driven Development (TDD) and systematic debugging frameworks.
🔌 Cross-harness compatibility supporting Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and more.

Give your AI agents the methodology they need to independently design specs, break tasks into manageable chunks, utilize git worktrees for isolation, write unit tests first, and execute robust refactoring cycles. 

Check out the repo and upgrade your workflow today:
https://github.com/obra/superpowers

🎬 Turn any complex technical topic into a fully narrated, code-drawn motion graphics explainer video with just a single prompt! 🚀

Tired of spending days editing videos to explain intricate software architecture, APIs, or documentation? 

Meet *anything2explainer* (https://github.com/Vincentwei1021/anything2explainer), an incredible open-source multi-agent workflow for AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Codex that automates the entire video production pipeline from scratch.

Here is how it solves the video creation bottleneck:
You simply provide a topic, length, and language. The system coordinates specialized AI agents to handle research, script writing, TTS voiceover generation with precise word-boundary alignment, storyboarding, and parallel code generation of Remotion components.

🔥 Key Features:
• Multi-Agent Division-of-Labour: Specialized agents coordinate for research, narration, parallel shot building, and automated quality control.
• Code-Driven Rendering: Uses Remotion, React, and TypeScript instead of fragile generative video models or stock footage.
• Perfect Synchronization: Frame-accurate timeline sync with text-to-speech voiceovers, automatic subtitles, and dynamic chapter tracking.
• Built-In Quality Control: Quantitative frame metrics and structured human-in-the-loop checkpoints ensure high visual accuracy.

Whether you are a developer advocate creating product walkthroughs, an AI engineer showcasing architectures, or a frontend dev wanting a reproducible, code-first video pipeline, this tool eliminates manual video editing completely.

🌪️ OpenAI just dropped a massive mathematical breakthrough on GitHub! 

OpenAI has open-sourced Lean 4 formalization certificates proving finite-time singularity blowups for the Navier-Stokes and Euler equations. 

For decades, mathematicians and physicists have wrestled with whether smooth solutions for fluid dynamics equations can break down in finite time. The problem? Human-verified proofs in advanced PDEs are notoriously prone to oversight. 

This repository solves that by delivering absolute, machine-checked mathematical certainty. 

Key Features:
• Lean 4 formalization certificates verifying the lack of global smooth solutions for Navier-Stokes in whole space and periodic torus environments.
• Machine-checked construction of smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free initial velocity for unforced Euler equations developing finite-time singularities.
• Seamless integration with Mathlib and Lake for building, caching, and independently verifying complex physics-based proofs.
• Support for independent proof checking via Comparator challenges.

Whether you are a formal verification researcher, a mathematician, or an advanced software engineer working with dependent type systems, this repo lets you study how to formalize high-dimensional PDEs in Lean 4 with zero human verification blind spots.

Stop wasting tokens on flat AI coding loops by structuring your coding agents into a hierarchical multi-model topology with Astra and Luna. 🚀

If you are an AI engineer or tech lead trying to scale automated workflows across complex codebases, you know the pain of burning through rate limits blindly on flat coding loops. 

The Codex Astra Luna Orchestrator solves this by providing a pre-configured multi-agent orchestration setup. It uses GPT-6 Astra as a high-level root orchestrator and reviewer, paired with GPT-5.6 Luna as specialized execution subagents for exploring, building, and testing code. 

✨ Notable Features:
• Hierarchical role distribution mapping specific reasoning models and effort levels (low, medium, max) to distinct duties like orchestration, execution, and independent review.
• Automated setup scripts for macOS, Linux, and Windows that seamlessly provision target repositories with correct configuration profiles and project-level agent skills.
• Built-in token usage tracking via a custom Python script that analyzes rollout logs under ~/.codex/sessions to measure consumption per thread, role, and model.
• Flexible profile switching supporting both Pro and Plus subscription tiers with tailored reasoning effort defaults and concurrent thread limits.

Whether you are implementing large features across multiple microservices by spinning up parallel worker subagents, or conducting deep repository refactoring with automated test verification, this framework gives you a structured way to execute larger features safely with independent code reviews built right in.

Check out the repository here:
https://github.com/donvito/codex-astra-luna-orchestrator

🤖 Bridge the gap between reinforcement learning simulation and physical hardware with an open-source, compact biped robot powered by a Raspberry Pi and ONNX policies!

Training walking policies in simulation is one thing, but deploying them to real-world edge hardware often means building a complex deployment stack from scratch. 

Microduck solves this by providing a complete, end-to-end hardware and software tutorial for building, configuring, and deploying reinforcement-learning-powered biped robots. 

Notable Features:
- Simulation-to-Real Pipeline: Uses an MjLab-based RL environment for training walking policies and exporting them directly to ONNX format.
- Edge Runtime on Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W: Runs Python deployment code to read IMU sensor data, process inputs, and drive a 14-servo Dynamixel bus via an OpenRB-150 controller.
- Headless Bluetooth Gamepad Service: Integrated systemd service for wireless teleoperation that automatically manages network states for 2.4GHz bandwidth.
- Reproducible OS Image Provisioning: Includes a pre-built Raspberry Pi OS Lite image with pre-configured Python virtual environments and automation services via a comprehensive Makefile.

Perfect for robotics engineers, RL researchers, and embedded systems developers looking to prototype low-cost hardware architectures or deploy custom locomotion models onto physical agents.

Check out the full repository and start building:
https://github.com/AI-FanGe/Microduck-build-tutorial
